headline: Light rain arrives Saturday evening and Sunday, then cooler, unsettled weather continues next week, possibly wetter Wednesday and Thursday.
summary: A weather system now near British Columbia moves south into western Washington Saturday evening. Rain should reach the coast first, then spread inland by Sunday morning. Forecasters expect it to be light, with the most falling along the coast and over the Olympics. Highs over the next few days should be in the mid to upper 50s. The large area of low pressure higher in the atmosphere driving this system keeps moving south Sunday into Monday. Most computer models take its center into Oregon, which would make Monday drier around here. If it tracks closer to the Oregon/Washington border, light showers could linger Monday. Overnight lows should rise from the low 30s to low 40s to the upper 30s to mid 40s by Monday. The rest of the week stays cooler and unsettled as more systems pass through. A broad dip in the jet stream is expected over the region Tuesday, with another low to the north. That low is expected to move south, and models are now trending wetter for Wednesday and Thursday, though those details could still shift. Highs next week should be in the low to mid 50s, with the coldest temperatures late in the week and lows in the low 30s to low 40s. No watches, warnings, or advisories are in effect for land areas. Small Craft Advisories for boaters cover the Pacific coastal waters and the Strait of Juan de Fuca until 5 PM Sunday, with seas building to 10 to 12 feet.
changes: The outlook was essentially unchanged. The later discussion added specific temperature ranges: highs in the mid to upper 50s now and low to mid 50s next week, plus warming overnight lows by Monday. It also gave start times for the boating advisories (between 3 PM and 8 PM Saturday).
